review_notes:
I reviewed all 55 lines of the file. It contains one declaration, `primeCancellation_polynomial_conductor`. This is a real-valued inequality that needs several hypotheses: `0 ≤ c`, `1 ≤ Q`, `0 < X` and `1 ≤ Real.log X`. Its conclusion, `primeCancellationWeight c (4*Q^2) X ≤ 25*heckeExponentialError (c/5) X Q`, says one quantity is bounded by another, so it cannot serve as a simp rewrite rule. It also has no canonical normal form to give simp.

The file adds no `@[simp]` attributes and the proof never calls `simp`. The proof uses `linarith`, `nlinarith`, `positivity`, `rw`, `unfold` and `convert ... using 1 <;> ring`. A search of the whole project finds only one use of the lemma, in `Angular/AngularPrimeFromPrimitive.lean` line 45, where it is applied directly as a term in an inequality argument rather than used in any simplification.

The local `hlogR` rewrite of `Real.log (4*Q^2)` is used only inside this proof. It specializes the existing `Real.log_mul` and `Real.log_pow` and is not a candidate for a general simp lemma. The file therefore has no simp interface: no simp lemmas, no simp sets and no simp-normal-form rewrites for this rubric to assess.
